Android 13+ can share audio to multiple LE Audio receivers on supported hardware. Open the output switcher and choose Audio sharing / Broadcast.
Android mainly allows one classic Bluetooth (A2DP) connection per phone. No app can change that limit. Dual Audio uses the multi-output features your phone actually has, and tells you when it cannot.

Useful when a device will not connect or when you want to check what your phone reports.
Dual Audio is open source and has no internet permission. It does not collect analytics. Shizuku is optional and only used locally.

Reality check: most phones physically support only one classic Bluetooth audio connection. This app unlocks the multi-output features that exist on your phone; it cannot add a feature the firmware does not have.
Android needs the Nearby devices permission to list and inspect your paired Bluetooth audio devices. No location data is used.

True dual Bluetooth audio depends on your phone, not just the app.

• Samsung Galaxy and some OEMs support two outputs in the system switcher.
• Android 13+ may support multiple LE Audio receivers.
• Other phones usually allow only one classic Bluetooth audio connection.

Dual Audio shows you exactly what your phone can do and helps you enable it.

Shizuku is a separate open-source app. It is not root.

1. Install Shizuku from the Play Store or GitHub.
2. Enable Developer options and Wireless debugging.
3. In Shizuku, tap “Start via Wireless debugging” and pair.
4. Return here and grant access.

When enabled, Dual Audio reapplies routing after a device reconnects or the audio policy resets.

Your phone reported:

%1$s

This usually means the phone allows only one Bluetooth audio connection. Try the system output switcher, or use two devices that support LE Audio sharing.

Android exposes a system output switcher and, on Android 12+, an internal “combined routing” API. The switcher is the safest path and is what Samsung uses for Dual Audio.\n\nDual Audio does not pretend to bypass hardware limits. If your phone’s Bluetooth stack only permits one A2DP link, the second device will disconnect and this app will tell you so.
